label: PF Backlog 339
title: OS/shell neutrality: remove PowerShell-only scripting/doc workarounds
body:
## Problem / why
Product Forge must be OS/shell-neutral. Some dev workflows, scripts and documented commands are currently expressed with PowerShell-specific constructs (heredocs, Out-String, `;` chaining, path quoting), which do not run on Linux/macOS CI or by contributors using bash/zsh.

## Goal & value
Make every scripted workflow and documented command cross-platform: pure Python entrypoints, a single shell-neutral invocation contract, no PowerShell-only syntax.

## In scope
- Audit scripts/dev/*, docs, PR/CI docs and agent prompts for PowerShell-specific commands.
- Replace PowerShell-only recipes with neutral `python ...` invocations (scripts as .py files, not heredocs).
- Add a guard (advisory) that flags PowerShell-only syntax in scripts/docs.
- Root-cause via RCCA where a PowerShell assumption caused a defect.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- All documented dev commands run under both bash and PowerShell (or are pure `python -m` invocations).
- No heredoc/Out-String/`;`-chaining requirements in docs/scripts.
- Guard reports 0 PowerShell-only occurrences (advisory allowlist for genuine examples).

## Notes
Surfaced while executing the master plan on Windows; scheduled AFTER master-plan phases complete. Product runtime is already pure Python; this is tooling/doc neutrality.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Audit (grep/ripgrep) scripts/dev/*, docs/, and agent prompt files for PowerShell-only constructs (Out-String, heredoc-style @'...'@, ;-chaining in documented commands, PS path quoting). Replace each recipe with a pure `python ...` / `python -m ...` invocation; scripts already exist as .py files so no new entrypoints are needed in most cases. ADD an advisory guard scripts/dev/ps_neutrality_check.py (mirroring the pattern of scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py) that flags PS-only syntax with an allowlist file for genuine examples. Run RCCA only where a PowerShell assumption caused an actual defect. Candidate components listed (core/api_docs.py, forge_constitution.py, etc.) are runtime modules - this item is tooling/doc-only, so no runtime component is modified.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES master-plan phases complete (item note: scheduled AFTER). Express as a soft sequencing constraint rather than a hard task dependency.
RELATED BI-PF-0408 - new global /pf command and help text must be written PS-neutral from the start.
RELATED BI-PF-1193 - /pf docs corrections should also be PS-neutral.
conflict_findings: Guard is a new file (scripts/dev/ps_neutrality_check.py) - no writer conflict.
Doc edits may overlap with BI-PF-1193 (/pf docs) and BI-PF-0408 (help text) - coordinate or sequence after them.
scripts/dev/* edits could collide with any concurrently active dev-script item; low likelihood, advisory guard only.
duplication_findings: No open backlog item performs a PS-neutrality audit/guard; BI-PF-0408 touches .opencode command files (possible PS in global command docs) - RELATED, keep consistent.
scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py is an existing guard pattern to mirror, not a duplicate.
Product runtime is already pure Python per the item - no overlap with runtime work.
analysis.rationale: Tooling/doc-only MODIFY of existing scripts and docs plus one new advisory guard, mirroring the established scripts/dev guard pattern. Low risk, broad but mechanical scope; scheduled after master-plan phases to avoid doc churn conflicts.
assumptions: Product runtime is already OS-neutral; only tooling and docs need work (per item note).
All needed functionality exists as .py entrypoints so PS recipes can be replaced, not rewritten in bash.
The guard is advisory and does not block CI initially.
risks: Broad audit surface (scripts, docs, prompts) may surface many findings - mitigate by advisory-first enforcement with an allowlist.
Allowlist can rot into a hiding place for real PS-only recipes - require justification strings per entry.
Sequencing risk: if done before master-plan phases finish, doc churn causes conflicts - the item already mandates scheduling after.
Some commands may be genuinely easier in PS on Windows contributor machines - the guard is advisory by design.
evidence: Item states the runtime is pure Python and the scope is tooling/doc neutrality.
scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py demonstrates the established advisory-guard pattern to mirror.
